🇬🇧 You genuinely could not make this up.

In June, John Healey resigned as Defence Secretary. His words: the Treasury "has been unwilling to commit the resources that the nation needs to defend the country," and the drift towards just 2.7% of GDP by 2030 could "make the country less safe." He walked on principle. The military had asked for ~£28bn; it was offered ~£13.5bn.

Five weeks later, Andy Burnham made him CHANCELLOR — head of the very Treasury he'd just blamed.

And now the ending. The Treasury has confirmed his first Budget, on 28 October, will NOT commit to 3% of GDP on defence by 2030 — the exact target he resigned over. It's been kicked down the road to a 2027 review.

Same man. Same target. Opposite decision — and this time, no one else to blame.

So either the danger he warned of was real, and the Chancellor is now knowingly leaving us exposed — or the resignation was never about the money. It was a well-timed exit that made him look principled just as a leadership contest brewed, and handed him the second most powerful job in the country weeks later.

Reform UK would fund our Armed Forces to meet the threats we actually face. Defence is the first duty of government — not a bargaining chip.
